sections.h2: What notice does a North Carolina landlord give before an eviction?
sections.html:
The notice depends on why the landlord wants possession. For a tenancy that is simply ending, the landlord gives a notice to quit sized to the rental period. For unpaid rent, the landlord makes a demand and waits ten days. For a lease violation, the landlord relies on the lease terms and the summary ejectment statute.

These rules come from three sections of Chapter 42 of the General Statutes: 42-14 for ending a tenancy, 42-3 for rent demands, and 42-26 for the grounds that support a court case.

If you own a rented house and want to sell it, the notice you give controls how quickly the house can be delivered empty. The schedule below is worth reading before you promise a buyer a closing date.

sections.h2: How many days of notice does each type of tenancy get?
sections.html:
The number of days follows the rental period. A week-to-week tenant gets the shortest notice and a year-to-year tenant gets the longest.

Type of tenancyNotice to quit under G.S. 42-14
Year to yearAt least one month before the end of the current year
Month to monthSeven days
Week to weekTwo days
Space rental for a manufactured homeAt least 60 days before the end of the current rental period

Source: G.S. 42-14, North Carolina General Assembly. A written lease with a fixed end date works differently: the tenant who stays past the term is a holdover, and that is one of the grounds in G.S. 42-26. Read the lease for any extra notice terms before you count days.

sections.h2: What is the notice for unpaid rent in North Carolina?
sections.html:
The landlord demands all past-due rent, and the tenant has ten days after that demand to pay it. If the tenant does not, the lease term is forfeited and the landlord may enter and dispossess the tenant through the court process. G.S. 42-3 applies to leases that fix a time for rent payment.

A late fee is a separate matter. Under G.S. 42-46, a fee may be charged only if rent is five calendar days or more late, with the first day counted as the day after the due date. For monthly rent the cap is fifteen dollars or five percent of the monthly rent, whichever is greater. For weekly rent it is four dollars or five percent, whichever is greater. A late fee may be imposed one time for each late payment.

  • The late fee cannot be taken out of the next month's rent so as to put that payment in default.
  • A late fee cannot be charged for failure to pay water or sewer services provided under G.S. 62-110(g).
  • If the rent is subsidized, the fee is figured on the tenant's share of the rent only.

sections.h2: What other reasons support a notice and a court case?
sections.html:
G.S. 42-26 gives three grounds for summary ejectment: the tenant holds over after the term expires, the tenant breaks a lease condition that ends the estate, or the tenant leaves the premises while in arrears. Anything outside those grounds needs a fresh look at the lease and the statute.

One limit stands out for landlords who also supply utilities. The statute says arrears for water, sewer or electric charges cannot be the basis for terminating a lease. If a tenant owes you utility money, you have to use a different route to collect it.

A breach claim works best when the lease spells out the condition and what ends the tenancy. Keep copies of the lease, any written demand, the dates you delivered it and proof of how you delivered it. The magistrate decides on a preponderance of the evidence, so documents matter.

sections.h2: What comes after the notice period runs out?
sections.html:
If the tenant is still in the house, the landlord files a complaint, and the clerk issues a summons that sets the court date no more than seven days after issuance, excluding weekends and legal holidays. That timeline is in G.S. 42-28.

The North Carolina Judicial Branch says small claims dates are set within 30 days of filing, and that eviction cases are usually heard within 10 to 15 days. Our North Carolina eviction process page follows the case from complaint to the sheriff's writ.

When the magistrate gives judgment for possession, the sheriff executes the writ. The sheriff must give the tenant notice of the approximate time, and the writ has to be executed within five days of the sheriff receiving it, under G.S. 42-36.2.

sections.h2: How does an eviction notice affect selling a rented house?
sections.html:
A tenant's notice schedule runs on its own clock, so a landlord who sells should plan the closing date around it. A buyer who wants the house empty needs the notice period, the court case and any appeal time to fit before closing.

  • With a month-to-month tenant, seven days of notice ends the tenancy, and removal of a tenant who stays goes through the court.
  • With a year-to-year tenant, the notice must reach the tenant at least a month before the end of the current year.
  • With a manufactured home space, plan for at least 60 days before the end of the rental period.

If the owner is behind on the mortgage and the house is foreclosed, a tenant under a rental agreement entered or renewed on or after October 1, 2007 may end the tenancy on at least 10 but no more than 90 days' notice after the sale date, according to G.S. 45-21.16A. The foreclosure notice of sale for a residential property with fewer than 15 rental units has to say that an order for possession may issue.

sections.h2: What should an owner write down before serving any notice?
sections.html:
Write down the type of tenancy, the rental period, the due date of rent and the dates of each payment. Then match those facts to the table above and the statute for your ground.

  • Which tenancy type applies and which notice period goes with it.
  • Whether the lease adds duties beyond the statute.
  • The exact date and way the notice or rent demand was delivered.
  • Whether any part of the amount claimed is water, sewer or electric arrears.
  • Whether a fee you want to charge is allowed under G.S. 42-46.

Ask the clerk of superior court in your county for the current complaint form and filing instructions, and ask an attorney who handles landlord matters to review a notice before you serve it.

faqs.q: How many days of notice does a month-to-month tenant get in North Carolina?
faqs.a: Seven days. G.S. 42-14 sets the notice to quit at seven days for a month-to-month tenancy, two days for week to week, and at least one month before the end of the year for a year-to-year tenancy.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to pay after a rent demand?
faqs.a: Ten days after the demand for all past-due rent. G.S. 42-3 says the lease term is forfeited if the tenant does not pay in that window, and the landlord may then enter and dispossess.

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict a tenant for unpaid water or electric bills?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 42-26 says arrears for water, sewer or electric charges cannot be the basis for lease termination, so those charges need a different collection route.

faqs.q: How much notice does a manufactured home space tenant get?
faqs.a: At least 60 days before the end of the current rental period, under G.S. 42-14. That is the longest periodic notice in the statute apart from the year-to-year rule.

faqs.q: Can I serve a notice and then change the locks myself?
faqs.a: No. Possession is delivered through a court judgment and a sheriff's writ, not through a notice alone. The summons for a complaint is set within seven days of issuance under G.S. 42-28, so the court step is quick once you file.
